item.title: Woman dies following incident in al Gaxaq
item.description: Newsbook has reported that a woman died following an incident in al Gaxaq. The incident occurred at about 2.30pm in Dawret al Gaxaq, where the street was closed to traffic, and the articles earlier text said the womans condition was not yet known. No further details on the cause or circumstances of the death had been released at the time of publication.

item.title: PN says government continues to hide the scale of Maltas waste problem
item.description: The Nationalist Party has accused the government of selectively presenting Maltas waste figures. The PN said the headline figure of 1,092 kg of waste per person in 2024, on which reports that Malta generates the least waste in the EU were based, excludes major categories of mineral waste including construction and demolition waste, a qualification stated in Eurostats own publication. It said residents deserve the full picture and that the government continues to bury the problem.

item.title: Pharmacies open on Sunday 8 November: full list published
item.description: Newsbook has published the list of pharmacies that will remain open on Sunday 8 November, when most pharmacies on the island are closed. The listing covers localities including Valletta and Floriana, il-Marsa and amrun, al Qormi, Birkirkara, Gira and San wann, giving each pharmacys address and telephone number for residents who need medicines while the majority of pharmacies are shut.

item.title: ADPD and Momentum slam zoo permits and question governments animal welfare commitment
item.description: ADPD and Momentum have accused the authorities of turning a blind eye to planning irregularities and animal welfare violations after two zoo decisions. The Planning Authority sanctioned unauthorised structures at the L-Arka ta No zoo in Siiewi and granted Montekristo Estate a zoo licence valid until October 2027, the latter despite Labours 2026 electoral pledge that no new licences would be issued to facilities keeping dangerous animals. The Animal Welfare Directorate granted the Montekristo permit despite the establishments history of controversy, the parties said, while ADPD argued that confining sentient animals for entertainment is unethical. Momentum has called on the government to explain how it will ensure compliance with its own manifesto commitments.

item.title: Maltese rescue volunteers train with international teams in Crete
item.description: Members of the Maltese Association of the Order of Maltas Search and Rescue Unit joined teams from Greece, Romania and Cyprus, plus the Italian CISOM corps, for the four-day TALOS 2026 exercise in Heraklion. The drills covered a night-time search and rescue scenario with the Maltese contingent operating alongside the international teams.

item.title: Maltese court orders four investment firms to pay Vatican Bank 24.1 million
item.description: The First Hall of the Civil Court has held four investment companies jointly and severally liable for damages over their handling of the Vatican Banks investment in the Kappa Fund and transactions involving Budapests former stock exchange. Optimum Evolution Fund SIF, Optimum Asset Management SA, Futura Investment Management Ltd and Futura Funds SICAV plc were found to have breached their fiduciary duties to the bank over the sale of the Exchange Palace, formally the Institute for World Trade. The companies were ordered to pay 24.1 million plus eight per cent interest.

item.title: Activists urge demolition of fake Bidnija sheep farm after court ruling
item.description: Moviment Graffitti has called on the Planning Authority to demolish a multi-storey building in Bidnijas Wied tal-ejjen that was approved as a sheep farm but stands in a valley outside the development zone with ecologically important freshwater habitats. The move follows the Court of Appeals rejection of the permit holders request for a retrial, leaving the revocation of his permit in place. The building, approved in 2019, includes reception areas and a swimming pool.

item.title: Pedestrian seriously injured after being hit by a motorbike in Mosta
item.description: A man suffered serious injuries after a Yamaha 125 motorbike struck him at about 3.45pm on Triq San Pawl tal-Qliega, Mosta, police said. The pedestrian, whose identity is not known, and the 25-year-old rider from St Pauls Bay were both taken to Mater Dei Hospital, with the motorcyclists condition still to be established. Police investigations are ongoing.

item.title: Christmas in the Capital 2026 to cost 750,000 with 300 artists across 25 events
item.description: The Valletta Cultural Agency will spend 750,000 on this years Christmas in the Capital programme, 100,000 more than last year. Some 300 artists take part in 25 events running from 25 November until New Years Eve, including the lighting of the Christmas tree outside Parliament, candlelight concerts, Carols in the Capital at St Francis Church and the traditional Baby Jesus procession on 17 December.

item.title: Government to review DC15 planning and design guidelines
item.description: Planning Minister Jonathan Attard announced at the close of the national property conference that a public consultation on the Development Control (DC15) design guidelines will be launched in the coming weeks, to address what he called ambiguities in the rules and place architectural quality and protected building heritage at the centre of development policy.

item.title: Mediterranean College of Sport opens primary school with 93 pupils
item.description: Education Minister Byron Camilleri inaugurated the colleges new primary level, where 93 pupils follow an academic programme alongside daily 45-minute sports sessions. The college, which opened in 2024 offering secondary and sixth-form education, now has more than 360 students and is expected to reach about 450 by the next scholastic year.

item.title: Food safety warning: chicken mince packets may contain bone fragments
item.description: The Food Safety Authority advised consumers not to eat 400g packets of Chefs Choice frozen chicken mince with use-by dates of 23 September 2027, 5 October 2027 and 23 October 2027, as they may contain excessive amounts of bone fragments. The alert followed information received from the operator; the product can be returned to the store or disposed of.

item.title: 20,000 ERA fine after protected Lija tree cut down despite warnings
item.description: The Environment and Resources Authority imposed a 20,000 administrative penalty after a strictly protected Southern nettle tree in Lija was felled on a plot earmarked for development. An arborist had alerted ERA days earlier and the authority had informed the projects architect that the tree was protected, but it was gone by the time officials inspected the site.

item.title: Terraced house asking prices up 104,000 in a year, KPMG finds
item.description: A KPMG study presented at the national property conference found the median asking price of a terraced house is now 725,000, up from 620,500 a year ago, while apartments rose about 10% to 350,000. Median apartment prices have climbed around 32% since 2019, and finished apartments are on average about 5% smaller than in 2024.

item.title: Suspected brothel pimp granted bail after woman testifies
item.description: Joseph Zammit, 50, of Marsaskala, was granted bail despite prosecution objections on nine charges including human trafficking, sexual exploitation and money laundering. A Colombian woman told the court she worked 12-hour shifts at a Fgura brothel, handling up to 14 clients a day while repaying a 4,000 travel debt, with half her earnings taken by Zammit plus 150 a week for accommodation.

item.title: Malta contributed 5.16 million to the EU Ukraine Facility in 2025
item.description: Foreign Minister Chris Fearne told parliament that Malta paid 5,159,221.11 into the EUs Ukraine Facility in 2025, about 1 million more than the 4.16 million Malta reported separately for humanitarian assistance that year. Most of that total was the countrys share of EU spending, with 279,676 channeled through the United Nations.

item.title: Momentum and ADPD challenge government over zoo licences
item.description: Momentum said the zoo licence granted to Montekristo Estate contradicts the Labour Partys 2026 electoral pledge that no new licences would be issued to facilities keeping dangerous animals, and called on the government to explain compliance and enforcement. ADPD-The Green Party also condemned the decision, pointing to the 57,000 fine paid by the directors of the so-called therapeutic zoo at Noahs Ark, and demanding transparency over the licensing process.

item.title: Maximilian Ciantar acquitted over knuckleduster found at Mater Dei
item.description: Maximilian Ciantar, the 2010 Attard road-rage case figure, was acquitted of possessing a knuckleduster at Mater Dei Hospital and of recidivism after prosecutors failed to summon the main witness. The court found the carer who allegedly saw him acting illegally and taking drugs was never called to testify, with prosecutors instead relying on two witnesses who described what the carer had told them. The knuckleduster was found in a cupboard, but police failed to prove it was Ciantars and had not read him his rights while questioning him.

Home Affairs Minister Glenn Bedingfield said police began investigating as soon as the first reports came in on Monday, and by Thursday officers had identified and detained the four suspects.

item.title: Geologists again excluded from amended excavation legislation
item.description: The Council of the Malta Chamber of Geologists said Legal Notice 305 of 2026, amending the third-party property damage regulations, again failed to give geologists a role in assessing ground and subsurface conditions and did not restore mandatory geological investigations. The chamber also criticised the Building and Construction Authority for not consulting it and said the 45-degree affected zone applies to soil rather than rock, in a sector where most excavations take place in rock.

item.title: Application seeks approval to replace century-old Valletta shopfront
item.description: An application has been filed to sanction the removal of a century-old, protected wooden shopfront in Valletta and replace it with a replica. The distinctive red timber facade of the former Raffaele Portelli 1917 shop, one of around 100 protected Valletta shopfronts, disappeared earlier this year. The application must now be considered by the Planning Authority.

item.title: Wied Dalam national park approved on former RAF fuel depot site in Birżebbuġa
item.description: The Planning Authority approved WasteServ Maltas application to turn a 34,000 square metre former RAF aviation fuel depot near Għar Dalam into Wied Dalam Park, administered by GreenServ. The plans keep the industrial heritage, including 26 ventilation shaft structures, and add picnic and play areas, more than 200 trees and 900 indigenous shrubs. The national park project had first been announced in 2017 while the site was still in use.

item.description: A valley in Luqa has been left coated in thick grey slurry after a spill from a nearby Polidano concrete batching plant. Maltas Rangers Unit flagged the affected valley and alerted ERA, which instructed the operator to carry out clean-up and corrective actions.

item.title: American who lived in Malta convicted of killing partner and baby daughter
item.description: An Italian court found Charles Francis Kaufmann, who legally changed his name to Rexal Ford and was known as Daniel R. Foster while living in Marsascala in 2022, guilty of the double murder of his partner Anastasia Trofimova and their 11-month-old daughter, plus concealment of a corpse. He was sentenced to life imprisonment with three years of solitary confinement. Maltese police were involved in the investigation because of his Maltese residence and his years on the island.

item.title: American who lived in Malta jailed for life over murder of partner and baby daughter
item.description: A 47-year-old American man who used multiple identities and lived in Marsaskala has been sentenced to life in prison by an Italian court for the murder of his partner and their 11-month-old daughter. Born Charles Francis Kaufmann, he used the name Rexal Ford and presented himself as a film director. The lifeless bodies of Anastasia Trofimova and their daughter Andromeda were found in Romes Villa Pamphili park in June 2025 after the family moved to Rome, and he was later convicted of double murder and concealment of a corpse.
